purpose: Consult before retrieving a source. Records what an agent found when it inspected a domain's robots file and terms, so the same check is not repeated by every author and so an exclusion one author discovered is not missed by the next. A verdict here does not replace the per-source check the rights policy requires; it tells you what was found before, and when. Re-verify anything older than the recheckAfterDays below, and append a domain the first time you check it.

domains.evidence: Terms page states the illustrations are free for any use, including educational, research, informational and commercial purposes, and directs the user to the licence on each entry for attribution requirements. No account needed. No robots.txt served.
domains.notes: Licence is per entry; sampled entries are labelled Public Domain. Record the per-entry label every time. Suggested credit form: Illustration from NIAID NIH BioArt Source (bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/###).

domains.evidence: Licences are stated per icon and span CC0, CC BY 3.0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA, MIT and BSD.
domains.notes: Only CC0 and CC BY 4.0 items qualify. CC BY 3.0 items are rejected as well as the share-alike ones.

domains.evidence: /wiki/File: and /wiki/Category: are crawlable; the /w/ API path is disallowed to crawlers but is a documented programmatic interface and was used with a descriptive User-Agent for licence lookup only, with every result confirmed on the human file page.
domains.notes: Licences are per file and most cell-biology diagrams are CC BY-SA, which this project rejects. Usable only for the CC0 and public-domain seam. Never a source for artwork whose creator has a canonical site of their own.

domains.evidence: robots.txt carries named blocks for GPTBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended, each with Disallow: /.
domains.notes: Only the robots file was fetched; no content was retrieved. This is the American Physiological Society's own platform, and the exclusion does not extend to APS articles deposited in PMC, which are reachable at pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/ and were used that way by PREM-BIO-005. Consequence recorded for the next author: Wright, Loo and Hirayama, Biology of human sodium glucose transporters, Physiological Reviews 91:733-794 (2011), is the standard reference for sodium-glucose cotransport energetics and is not in PMC, so its full text is unreachable under these rules. Gyimesi et al. 2020 in Pflugers Archiv (PMC7462921, CC BY 4.0) and Koepsell 2020 (PMC7462918, CC BY 4.0) between them carry the stoichiometry and driving-force statements that review is usually cited for.

domains.notes: Do not open /books/. Four separate lesson authors reached this independently.

domains.notes: The route to use for PMC full text.

domains.notes: One author requested it before reading the rule to the end, discarded the value, and removed the claims depending on it.

domains.evidence: robots.txt sets User-agent: ClaudeBot with Disallow: /.
domains.notes: Not fetched, so the content licence is unverified. Access rules are checked before licence questions.

domains.evidence: Terms of use section 3, User Obligations, requires the user to "Not use automated methods (bots, scrapers, etc.) to access or download Site Content". The CC BY 4.0 licence on the medical images is real and confirmed on individual item pages, and the terms treat site chrome and the images as separate categories, but the obligation is written broadly enough to cover access and download. robots.txt separately disallows /*?s=, /search/ and /*filter-tag=.
domains.notes: Human-only. An agent may not fetch from this host; a person may, and the images remain usable under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution wording Servier publishes. A licence to reuse is not permission to automate retrieval, and the two are recorded separately here for that reason. Practical note for cell biology: the intracellular-component PNGs are icon-sized, median about 234 by 108 pixels, and no standalone whole-cell figure exists in the library; the only annotated whole cell sits inside a PowerPoint set. Do not take Servier assets from Wikimedia Commons, where the same art is mirrored under a superseded CC BY-SA 3.0.

domains.evidence: Website terms 5.2 and 5.4 prohibit text and data mining including development, training, fine-tuning or validation of AI systems, and withhold consent for such use.
domains.notes: robots permits the chapter paths; the prohibition is in the terms, not robots. Found only by reading the terms.

domains.notes: Only fetch a file here after reading its licence on the corresponding commons.wikimedia.org file page.

domains.notes: Excluded because unverified, not because terms were found wanting. Re-check before use and record the result.

domains.evidence: robots.txt is a 527-entry blocklist of named bad bots, each carrying Disallow:/, with the header comment recording its version and that count. It contains no User-agent: * block and names neither ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai nor GPTBot, so no rule here excludes an agent of this kind; CCBot is present and disallowed. The terms of use at /about/policies/terms-of-use permit review, reproduction or translation of extracts for research or private study, require acknowledgment of WHO as the source with the URL, and prohibit sale, commercial use, and reproduction of substantial portions without prior written authorisation. No text-and-data-mining or AI-training clause was found.
domains.notes: Restricted on licence rather than on access. Nothing here is openly licensed: the terms are attribution plus non-commercial, which sits outside this project's accepted reuse set, so the only available rights basis is facts-only-original-expression. Read a fact, write your own sentence, and do not carry WHO wording into a lesson. Practical caution found by PREM-BIO-005: the cholera fact sheet's case-fatality figure is written as a programmatic target for treatment centres and not as a measured before-and-after, so it does not support a claim that any therapy achieved that number. That lesson used a CC BY journal source for the figure instead and cited no WHO page.

domains.evidence: Serves no robots file of its own; www.nist.gov/robots.txt applies and permits /div898/.
domains.notes: The NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook.

domains.evidence: robots.txt disallows the legacy /pmc/articles route for unnamed agents. The wildcard User-agent block was read in full on 2026-07-27: it disallows /pmc/articles/ but the only /books/ rule in it is Disallow: /books/?term=, which covers the Bookshelf search query string and not the /books/NBK... record paths. No AI-specific crawler is named anywhere in the file, so the wildcard block governs.
domains.notes: Use pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/ instead for PMC articles, which robots explicitly allows. The /books/NBK... Bookshelf route is separately permitted and is the route PREM-BIO-004 and PREM-BIO-005 used for Molecular Biology of the Cell chapters. Two cautions on that route. Bookshelf pages for that title display 'By agreement with the publisher, this book is accessible by the search feature, but cannot be browsed', which is a publisher limit on paging through the work rather than a prohibition on retrieving a permitted page; retrieve the specific section you cite and no more. And the book is conventionally copyrighted, not openly licensed, so the only rights basis available is facts-only-original-expression: take the fact, write your own sentence. Table content is frequently not served on those pages, only a thumbnail link, so a table's numbers cannot be read this way and must not be reconstructed from memory.

domains.evidence: robots.txt permits the health-information paths used.

The Image and Video Gallery applies one blanket licence to every item: Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial ShareAlike 3.0. NonCommercial and ShareAlike are both outside this project's accepted licence set.
domains.notes: Excluded on licence, not on access. Being an NIH gallery does not make the contents public domain. images.nigms.nih.gov no longer resolves; the gallery lives under www.nigms.nih.gov/image-gallery.

domains.evidence: robots.txt names ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai in their own blocks, each with Disallow: /, alongside GPTBot, CCBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, ChatGPT-User, Bytespider, meta-externalagent and roughly a dozen other AI agents. The User-agent: * block does permit article paths, but a named agent block governs over the wildcard, so the exclusion applies.
domains.notes: Not fetched. Consequence for authors: a Lancet item can be established bibliographically through pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, which gives title, journal, year, volume, pages and PMID, but its text cannot be read here and so cannot be the source of a claim. PREM-BIO-005 wanted the 1978 editorial 'Water with sugar and salt' and found two secondary sources quoting its best-known line differently, which is exactly the failure mode a second-hand quotation invites; the lesson dropped the quotation rather than repeat one it could not read.

domains.evidence: robots.txt disallows GPTBot.
domains.notes: The ASA statement on p-values is reachable instead from the ASA's own release of it.

domains.evidence: The host serves no robots.txt of its own (HTTP 404), so www.nist.gov/robots.txt governs, following the same reasoning already recorded here for www.itl.nist.gov. That file's wildcard block disallows administrative, search, user-account and Drupal scaffolding paths only; it does not disallow /cgi-bin/cuu/ or any other fundamental-constants path, and it names no AI-specific crawler, so no agent-specific rule applies.
domains.notes: The route for CODATA recommended values of the fundamental constants, one value per page at /cgi-bin/cuu/Value?<symbol>. Each page states the value, the unit, the standard uncertainty or the word exact, and the CODATA adjustment year, which is what a lesson quoting a constant needs. Since the 2019 SI redefinition the molar gas constant and the Faraday constant are both exact, so quote them as exact rather than attaching an uncertainty they no longer have.

domains.evidence: robots.txt permits the record paths this project reads and disallows bulk retrieval paths; no account is required to read an abstract record. NCBI's usage policy asks that scripted access run outside peak US hours and stay under three requests per second, and that a tool and contact be identified.
domains.notes: Abstract records only, and one at a time. Read it as a bibliographic check — a title, journal, year, DOI and abstract — not as the source of a claim: the abstract is a summary written to persuade a reader to open the paper, and figures quoted there are sometimes uncorrected. Where a record carries a correction notice, the corrected values live in the publisher's text, so prefer pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov for anything a lesson will assert. Never use it to retrieve an illustration; it hosts none that are ours to reuse.

domains.evidence: A request for /robots.txt returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, with the error document itself also failing, so no robots file could be read and no access terms could be established.
domains.notes: Excluded because unverified, not because terms were found wanting, following the precedent already recorded here for visualsonline.cancer.gov. Consequence recorded for the next author: Lee-Six et al., The landscape of somatic mutation in normal colorectal epithelial cells, Nature 574:532-537 (2019), is the colon counterpart of the normal-tissue mutation work and is not deposited in PMC, so its full text is unreachable under these rules. PREM-BIO-010 wanted it to keep its tissue-context argument inside the colon, could not read it, and used Martincorena et al. 2015 on normal human skin instead while stating in prose, in its claim uncertainty and in ATTRIBUTION.md that the evidence is skin rather than colon. Re-check before use and record the result.

domains.evidence: A request for /robots.txt was answered with an HTTP 302 redirect to misuse.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/error/abuse.shtml, so the robots file could not be read and the host's automated-access terms could not be established from it. NCBI's published usage policy for E-utilities asks that scripted access identify a tool and contact, stay under three requests per second, and run outside peak US hours.
domains.notes: Used by PREM-BIO-010 for two esummary requests that mapped PubMed identifiers to PMC identifiers, with a tool name and contact supplied, before its robots file had been requested. It is the source of no claim in that pack: every identifier it returned was confirmed by opening the article on pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, which is the allowed route. Because the robots response was an abuse-notice redirect, treat this host as not verified and prefer pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov for bibliographic checks, one record at a time, which the ledger already records as allowed. Do not use it in bulk.
